newsitem.title: USA: US House tax panel to consider tax bill next week.
newsitem.headline: US House tax panel to consider tax bill next week.

text.p: The House Ways and Means Committee is expected to consider tax legislation next week to implement the outline of the budget agreement reached last month between the White House and Republican Congressional leaders, a committee spokesman said on Friday.
All tax legislation must originate in the House.

The budget pact called for $85 billion net tax cuts over five years. The tax bill is widely expected to include a capital gains tax cut, a $500 per child tax credit, a college tuition tax credit, estate tax relief and expanded Individual Retirement Accounts.
The committee spokesman would not comment on the content of the legislation.

House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, a Texas Republican, said in a statement: "Over the next two weeks, this committee will work to provide tax relief so that American workers and families will be able to keep more of the money they make to save, invest, send their children to college, or spend as they see fit."
A congressional staffer said the legislation would be "a good faith effort to balance all of the interests of everybody."
